intro: Genesis gives a man named Enoch only four verses. It says he walked with God, and then God took him. Centuries later, Jewish writers composed a long book in his name. That book, 1 Enoch, told a much bigger story about heavenly beings called Watchers who came down to earth before the flood. For hundreds of years the whole book was kept only in Ethiopia. Then in 1773 it reached Europe, and in the 1950s pieces of it turned up among the Dead Sea Scrolls.

Researchers have studied this book closely. J. T. Milik published its Aramaic pieces from Qumran in 1976. George Nickelsburg and James VanderKam made a new English translation in 2004. Loren Stuckenbruck studied the Book of Giants, and Michael Heiser read 1 Enoch as a window into how many Jews read Genesis 6. In this unit you will read what 1 Enoch says, learn how it survived, and compare it with Genesis 6, Jubilees and Josephus. You will also test the idea that the story answered Babylon's tales of wise beings before the flood.

By the end you will be able to name the five parts of 1 Enoch and tell where the book is Scripture. You will be able to retell the Watchers story calmly and accurately. You will be able to explain two readings of Genesis 6, name who held them, and check a claim about Enoch against the texts themselves.
bigQuestion: What is 1 Enoch, and how does its story of the Watchers help readers understand Genesis 6 and the world of the New Testament?

timeline.t: Oldest parts of 1 Enoch, the Book of the Watchers and the Astronomical Book, begin to be written
The Dream Visions (1 Enoch 83–90) are written around the time of the Maccabean revolt
The book of Jubilees retells Genesis and tells of Enoch and the Watchers
The Parables (1 Enoch 37–71), the youngest part, are likely written
The letter of Jude quotes 1 Enoch 1:9 (Jude 14–15)
Josephus's Antiquities of the Jews retells Genesis 6 with angels of God
1 Enoch is translated into Ge'ez in Ethiopia (estimates vary)
James Bruce brings Ge'ez copies of 1 Enoch from Ethiopia to Europe
R. H. Charles's English translation of 1 Enoch appears in a popular edition
J. T. Milik publishes the Aramaic pieces of Enoch from Qumran Cave 4
George Nickelsburg publishes his commentary on 1 Enoch
Michael Heiser publishes Reversing Hermon, on Enoch and the Watchers

words.d: the oldest book written in Enoch's name, made of five parts from about 300 BCE to the first century CE
an ancient language of Ethiopia in which 1 Enoch survives complete
the list of books a religious community accepts as its Scripture
ancient writings credited to a famous past figure who did not write them; a scholars' label, not an insult
ancient Jewish manuscripts found near Qumran, 1947–1956, including Aramaic pieces of 1 Enoch
in 1 Enoch, heavenly beings, especially the two hundred who came down to earth
in Hebrew bene ha'elohim; in Job, heavenly beings; in Genesis 6:2, readers debate who they are
a debated Hebrew word in Genesis 6:4; the Septuagint translated it as giants
a tall mountain at the north of ancient Israel where, in 1 Enoch 6, the Watchers swear their oath
a Greek word for a deep prison; 2 Peter 2:4 uses a verb from it for where sinning angels are held
in Mesopotamian tradition, seven wise beings before the flood who were said to have taught people
a text written to challenge or answer another view

test.q: What does Genesis 5:24 say happened to Enoch?
choices: He walked with God and "was not," for God took him
test.why: Genesis 5:24 says Enoch walked with God and God took him.

test.q: Which part of 1 Enoch contains the story of the Watchers?
choices: The Book of the Watchers, chapters 1–36
test.why: The Watchers story is in the Book of the Watchers, 1 Enoch 1–36.

test.q: Which churches count 1 Enoch as Scripture?
choices: The Ethiopian and Eritrean Orthodox Tewahedo churches
test.why: 1 Enoch is canonical only in the Ethiopian and Eritrean Orthodox Tewahedo churches.

test.q: What did James Bruce do in 1773?
choices: He found the Dead Sea Scrolls
He brought Ge'ez copies of 1 Enoch from Ethiopia to Europe
test.why: Bruce returned from Ethiopia with copies of 1 Enoch in Ge'ez.

test.q: Which part of 1 Enoch has not been found among the Dead Sea Scrolls?
test.why: No piece of the Parables (chapters 37–71) has been found at Qumran.

test.q: Which New Testament letter quotes 1 Enoch 1:9?
How did the Septuagint translate the Hebrew word Nephilim?
test.why: The Greek Septuagint used gigantes, giving the King James Version its "giants."

test.q: Who leads the two hundred Watchers in 1 Enoch 6?
test.why: 1 Enoch 6 names Shemihazah, spelled Semjaza in Charles's translation.

test.q: In 1 Enoch 8, what does Azazel teach people?
test.why: 1 Enoch 8 says Azazel taught the making of weapons, jewelry and eye makeup.

test.q: Which four angels bring the earth's cry to God in 1 Enoch 9?
test.why: 1 Enoch 9:1 names Michael, Uriel, Raphael and Gabriel.

test.q: What is the Sethite view of Genesis 6?
choices: The sons of God were Babylonian sages
The sons of God were heavenly beings
The sons of God were men from Seth's family line
test.why: Augustine and many later Christians read the sons of God as men from Seth's line.

test.q: What did J. T. Milik publish in 1976?
choices: The Aramaic pieces of Enoch from Qumran Cave 4
The first English translation of 1 Enoch
test.why: Milik's The Books of Enoch (1976) published the Aramaic Enoch fragments from Qumran Cave 4.

test.q: What were the apkallu in Mesopotamian stories?
choices: Angels in the book of Tobit
Wise beings before the flood said to have taught people
test.why: The apkallu were seven sages before the flood in Mesopotamian tradition.

test.q: Which scholars argued that the Watchers story answered Babylon's apkallu stories?
choices: James Bruce and R. H. Charles
test.why: Annus (2010) compared the Watchers with the apkallu, and Heiser built on this in Reversing Hermon (2017).

test.q: Which verse uses a word from Tartarus for where sinning angels are held?
test.why: 2 Peter 2:4 uses a verb built from Tartarus.

write.prompt: Who were the sons of God in Genesis 6? Cite Genesis 6:1–4, 1 Enoch 6–10 and either Jude 6 or 2 Peter 2:4. Explain what each text says. Then compare two readings, such as the heavenly-beings reading of 1 Enoch and Josephus and the Sethite reading of Augustine, and name a modern scholar who studied the question.
tips: Name each text with book, chapter and verse, and say which translation you used.
Attribute every reading: "1 Enoch tells…", "Josephus wrote…", "Augustine read…", "Annus argued…".
Compare the readings fairly instead of judging which one is true.
Use the unit's terms, such as Watchers, Nephilim, sons of God and Septuagint.
Remember that 1 Enoch is Scripture for some churches and a historical source for others.
